cases.title: The Davies Sisters｜成长背景与收藏起点

paragraphs.label: 原文第1段
paragraphs.text: Gwendoline (1882-1951) and Margaret (1884-1963) Davies were the granddaughters of David Davies, a Welshman who amassed a fortune in the shipping and mining industries. In 1907, when Gwendoline came into her inheritance (Margaret would follow in 1909), the sisters were said to be the wealthiest unmarried women in Britain. Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.

paragraphs.label: 原文第2段
paragraphs.text: While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits. Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.

paragraphs.label: 原文第3段
paragraphs.text: The sisters began to make regular art purchases from 1908, which roughly coincided with the dates of their inheritance. They took advice from various people, including the art dealer Hugh Blaker (the brother of Jane Blaker) and David Croal Thompson, who was also an art dealer. While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

paragraphs.label: 原文第4段
paragraphs.text: The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master** paintings. Yet they initially made very few attempts to secure any such works. While the sisters were wealthy in relative terms, their income was nothing compared to the fortunes of American art collectors of this period, such as J. Pierpont Morgan. Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them. Instead, their early purchases were of the fashionable, safe variety, and included, for example, paintings by the French artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot.

structure: 这一部分把姐妹收藏艺术的起点放回家庭财富、成长教育与个人选择中理解：遗产提供条件，社会责任感影响用途，文化教育培养兴趣；她们听取顾问意见，却也有自己的判断。最后一段进一步说明，有购买能力、有个人偏好和愿意支付某个价格，是三个不同层面。
原文第1段：姐妹的财富来自祖父经营航运和采矿积累的资产，两人分别在1907年和1909年继承遗产。文中用were said to be转述她们当时被认为是英国最富有的未婚女性，而不是给出精确财富排名。宗教教养和威尔士乡村成长环境使她们产生社会责任感，因此她们选择把钱用于文化和慈善。财富来源与财富用途在这里被连接起来。
原文第2段：家中没有明确的艺术收藏传统，但姐妹接受的教育为这类兴趣准备了条件。学校重视文化学习，她们又随家庭女教师旅行、参观画廊、详细记录藏品。这里的such pursuits回指艺术收藏一类的文化活动；作者强调兴趣可以通过教育和接触逐渐形成，并不一定来自家族收藏传统。
原文第3段：从1908年起，她们开始规律购画，时间大致与继承遗产相近。两位艺术商提供建议，但对他们影响的理解后来发生了变化：过去常把收藏风格主要归于男性顾问，较新的看法则认为姐妹在选择中比人们原先承认的更主动。最后一句区分的是两种历史解释，并没有否定顾问确实提供过帮助。
原文第4段：日记显示姐妹喜欢欧洲早期大师的作品，可是最初很少购入。原因不是没有兴趣，而是她们虽富裕，与美国大收藏家的财力仍有差距。高质量作品即使并非完全买不起，也超过她们愿意支付的价格，所以早期购藏偏向当时流行、较稳妥的作品。Instead承接前面的现实限制，解释实际购买如何偏离个人偏好。

sentences.text: While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

cases.title: The Davies Sisters｜印象派转向与战时收藏

paragraphs.label: 原文第5段
paragraphs.text: However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***. We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris. Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet. Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.

paragraphs.label: 原文第6段
paragraphs.text: The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection. Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area. Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.

paragraphs.label: 原文第7段
paragraphs.text: It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health. Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery. Here she acquired two works by Cézanne - Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam. The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.

原文第5段：收藏方向改变后，姐妹开始购入法国印象派作品。支持当代法国艺术的Hugh Blaker参与了这个决定，她们在巴黎旅行时也应当接触过相关作品，但作者没有断言某一个因素就是决定性原因。1912年她们购入莫奈的威尼斯风景，之后12年形成了印象派收藏的主体。the bulk强调大部分藏品在这一时期积累。

cases.title: The Davies Sisters｜收藏停止与文化遗产

paragraphs.label: 原文第8段
paragraphs.text: Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

paragraphs.label: 原文第9段
paragraphs.text: By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

paragraphs.label: 原文第10段
paragraphs.text: The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

structure: 这部分先重新解释姐妹看似偏离艺术圈的生活方式，再说明战争造成的社会问题如何改变她们的支出重点，最后评价收藏留下的公共文化遗产。独立品味、社会责任与文化贡献在结尾汇合。
原文第8段：评论者常把姐妹描述为出人意料的收藏先驱，因为她们住在威尔士乡间，也不与艺术家或画廊主人交朋友。作者随后补充另一面：远离潮流压力使她们能够追随自己的品味。她们仍依赖可信顾问，经常到伦敦和巴黎，也让人把画送到家里考虑，因此地理上的偏远不等于缺少接触作品的机会。
原文第9段：到1920年代初，战争遗留的贫困和社会动荡使格温多琳对继续购画越来越不安。她把精力几乎完全转向社会事业，并将家宅发展为会议及音乐诗歌节场所，1926年作了最后一次购画。玛格丽特也在大致同期停止收藏，却在1930年代恢复小规模购买当代英国作品。两人的后续选择有关联，但不能合并为完全相同的人生轨迹。
原文第10段：文章把个人经历放回当时的艺术接受环境：姐妹收藏印象派时，个人和机构普遍忽视这类作品。她们的藏品后来分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，包含重要画家的代表作。最后一句评价她们追随个人喜爱的行为产生了超出私人范围的长期文化价值。

cases.title: Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A Humans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: B The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: C The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

cases.title: Why we need silence｜漂浮舱的两项实验

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: D Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health. One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation. While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist. 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains. 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein. 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'

paragraphs.label: E（第一段）
paragraphs.text: E To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session. Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.

paragraphs.label: E（第二段）
paragraphs.text: Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain. To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined. Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial. Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression. Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.

questions.evidence: the ability to focus on the breath

questions.explanation: general对应overall；答案是整体状态wellbeing，不是症状pain。

questions.evidence: a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression
questions.explanation: associated with对应linked with；48人/90分钟与上一项50人/一小时必须分开。

structure: 这一部分围绕漂浮舱提出两个层次的问题：人主观上有什么感受，脑活动发生了什么变化。文章分别介绍问卷与脑扫描研究，并保留科学解释中的不确定性；参与者报告的轻松感不能直接扩大成对所有疾病或所有人的疗效结论。
D：漂浮舱通过遮光、隔音和盐水漂浮减少外界感觉输入。有人会听见轻微嗡鸣或出现视觉感受，Feinstein认为这可能是大脑在缺少外界刺激时尝试填补空白。这些现象在他的描述中是良性的；真正帮助进入放松状态的，是把注意力放在呼吸上的能力。本段是在介绍一种体验及专家解释，并非要求读者自行进行治疗。
E（第一段）：研究团队招募50名有不同压力相关状况的人，在一次漂浮前后填写问卷。参与者报告一小时后肌肉紧张、疼痛和相关症状减少，放松感与整体舒适感提高。这里的信息来自参与者的前后自报；本段没有交代对照条件或长期追踪，因而只宜理解为此次研究中观察到的短时体验变化。
E（第二段）：第二项研究改为考察大脑：48人分别接受三次90分钟漂浮或在躺椅上放松，并在研究开始和结束时做功能磁共振扫描。原文报告只有漂浮组出现默认模式网络活动降低，该网络常与抑郁有关。Feinstein把这解释为可能帮助神经系统重获平衡的线索；seem和resetting上的引号提醒读者，这是一种试探性、形象化解释，不等于已经证明能治疗抑郁。

cases.title: Why we need silence｜主动安静与短时收益

paragraphs.label: F（第一段）
paragraphs.text: F Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy. 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains. 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'

paragraphs.label: F（第二段）
paragraphs.text: Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience. 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says. 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: G Eric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress. 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says. Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits. And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think. First, complete silence isn't necessary. In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room. Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits. 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says. 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week. Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'

questions.explanation: 必须有两种环境的比较；G中花园与完全静音房间的结果符合题干。

cases.instructions: Q17：Which section A–G contains the information? Q22/25/26：Match statements with people A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

structure: 安静在这里不是越彻底、越久就越好。文章强调个人意愿、当前心理状态和适应过程，再把理想化的绝对无声，转化为日常中较容易获得的短暂安静。
F（第一段）：Ben-Soussan把安静区分为外部环境的安静与内在状态的安静。她认为后者可以帮助人更清楚地觉察周围情况，并作出合宜反应。This承接这种内外安静的状态，而不是单指没有任何声音；本段呈现的是她对安静作用的解释。
F（第二段）：文章马上加入限制：不同人的获益程度不一样，而且主动愿意参与体验很重要。volition与intentionality指个人的意愿和有意识的参与。如果一个人并不想处于安静之中，这种情境反而可能令人痛苦。因此，安静不能被当成不顾意愿、对所有人都适用的要求。
G：Pfeifer进一步指出，高度紧张的人有时无法在安静环境中放松，专业指导可以帮助其逐渐适应。他随后提出两个让安静更可获得的想法：不必绝对无声，研究参与者在安静花园中比完全无声的房间更放松、较少无聊；也不必每次持续很久。他倾向于频繁短时的安静，但原文用likely表达判断，并未给出对所有人有效的固定时长处方。

phrases.explanation: heightened修饰state所指的程度，描述当时状态，不能直接给某人贴上永久性标签。

cases.title: The World of Sugar｜全球贸易与误解纠正

paragraphs.label: 原文第1段
paragraphs.text: Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

paragraphs.label: 原文第2段
paragraphs.text: Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

paragraphs.label: 原文第3段
paragraphs.text: The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

structure: 这是一篇书评的开头：作者介绍Bosma如何把糖写成一部全球贸易史和劳动史。甘蔗糖与甜菜糖、进口来源的变化、大种植园与小农生产相互补充，使糖的历史不再只剩单一地区或单一劳动制度。
原文第1段：书评首先评价这是一部真正具有全球范围的糖史，既讨论古巴和爪哇等甘蔗糖出口地，也把欧洲、美国的甜菜糖纳入。随后指出补贴与人为压低的价格会影响世界市场，威胁甘蔗糖生产者的生计。It指甜菜糖这一行业和产品，不能理解为世界上所有糖生产都采用同一制度。
原文第2段：英国市场的进口变化展示了全书的跨度：先从依赖奴役劳动的本国殖民种植园购买甘蔗糖，废奴后仍从保留奴隶制的古巴、巴西等地进口，19世纪末开始进口欧洲甜菜糖，20世纪才发展本国甜菜糖业。这段揭示，某国法律改变与商品供应链中的劳动制度变化并不一定同步。
原文第3段：作者转向劳动组织的多样性，纠正甘蔗糖始终只由富人拥有的大型专门种植园生产这一单一想象。爪哇的小农曾以高度劳动密集的方式同时种甘蔗和水稻，是这种多样性的一个实例。not just restricted强调不只存在大种植园，并没有否认大种植园的重要历史。

phrases.meaning: 以人为压低的价格出售
phrases.explanation: artificially在这里指价格受到补贴等外部干预，不是说产品是假货；at引出出售价格。
livelihood指赖以谋生的方式和收入基础；此处现在分词说明低价竞争带来的影响。
following相当于after，标记时间关系；它本身不保证其他国家或供应链也同时发生同样变化。
用于引入与常见理解不一致的事实，后面需要具体内容或例证支持，不能只把自己的意见写成事实纠正。

phrases.meaning: 一种极为依赖大量劳动投入的方式
phrases.explanation: labour-intensive描述生产对劳动投入的依赖程度，与单纯技术先进或落后不是同一个概念。

sentences.text: It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.
sentences.translation: 甜菜糖还获得了巨额补贴，并在世界市场上以人为压低的价格出售，威胁着甘蔗糖生产者的生计。
sentences.explanation: It承接上句的beet sugar；has been统领subsidised和sold两个被动分词。at引出价格，on world markets说明交易范围。末尾threatening...是补充结果的现在分词短语，说明受影响的是甘蔗糖生产者，而非把两种糖当成同一种生产群体。

sentences.text: For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.
sentences.translation: 例如，在20世纪初的重要食糖出口地爪哇，小农以极其劳动密集的方式，把甘蔗与水稻一起种植。
sentences.explanation: 主干是sugar cane was grown...by small farmers。a huge exporter...是Java的同位语，交代地区背景；together with rice说明共同种植的作物，in...way说明生产方式。句子把出口规模大与生产者是小农放在一起，说明两者可以同时成立。

cases.title: The World of Sugar｜劳动组织与行业权力

paragraphs.label: 原文第4段
paragraphs.text: The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

paragraphs.label: 原文第5段
paragraphs.text: This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

questions.prompt: In the big industries in both Germany and the US, sugar farming depended on 31 __________.
questions.evidence: German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production
questions.explanation: 波兰人赴德、墨西哥人等赴美均是跨地迁移劳工，概括为migrant workers。

questions.prompt: However, in other parts of the world such as South Asia and Latin America, 32 __________ continued.
questions.evidence: traditional methods on small farms
questions.explanation: small farms与small-scale cultivation对应；F outdated带有落后评价，原文只说traditional。

questions.prompt: Sugar production has also involved 33 __________ who were eager to protect their markets.
questions.evidence: a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations
questions.explanation: 资本家、糖业家族与公司合并概括为powerful individuals and businesses。

questions.prompt: In countries such as Cuba the sugar industry therefore had a major influence on 34 __________.
questions.evidence: Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states
questions.explanation: policies of states和politics对应national governments，不是农业技术。

questions.prompt: To support the interests of sugar producers, 35 __________ were established.
questions.evidence: their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies
questions.explanation: 贸易壁垒与补贴是financial controls的实例，不能只靠相同词选项。

questions.prompt: As a result of this, 36 __________ were penalised.
questions.evidence: it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse
questions.explanation: poor countries对应less wealthy nations，came off worse对应were penalised。

structure: 这部分将糖业的连续性放在两个层面观察：劳动者的处境和传统生产方式延续，资本、企业与国家政策的关系也长期存在。书评由田间劳动转向政治经济，解释谁能够保护自己的利益，谁更容易承担代价。
原文第4段：德国甜菜业、美国糖业都使用跨境劳工，说明不同地区的规模生产有相似的劳动力来源。作者继而指出，在文中所说的许多地方，砍甘蔗仍是报酬低、劳动艰苦的工作。另一种连续性是小农传统方法的延续，20世纪中叶在南亚和拉丁美洲占重要地位。连续性既指劳动处境，也指生产形式，不能把两者缩成同一个现象。
原文第5段：镜头从工人和农户转到资本家、糖业家族与长期有影响力的公司。书评认为，强大的糖业利益集团参与政治，并通过贸易壁垒和补贴保护自身利益；争夺行业控制权时，较穷国家更容易处于不利地位。最后一句是书评作者对Bosma叙述细致程度的赞赏，与前面概括的经济历史内容属于不同层次。

phrases.explanation: similarity比较不同地方或群体，continuity关注跨时间的持续；两词并列组织本段的观察角度。

phrases.phrase: a poorly paid and brutal business
phrases.meaning: 一种报酬低且极为艰苦的营生
phrases.explanation: business在这里指谋生活动，brutal强调劳动处境严酷；不是泛指某家公司。

phrases.phrase: remained influential over very long periods
phrases.meaning: 在很长时期内持续具有影响力
phrases.explanation: remain后接形容词，说明状态持续；over very long periods突出跨越时间的力量。
两者都是影响市场的政策工具，但机制不同：前者限制外部竞争，后者提供支持；其具体后果需要结合行业和政策设计讨论。

phrases.meaning: 在竞争或冲突中处于更不利的结果
phrases.explanation: come off是表示结果的短语动词，worse说明相对劣势；这里指贫穷国家在行业权力争夺中的处境。

sentences.text: In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies.
sentences.translation: 在许多地方——不只是英属加勒比地区，也包括古巴和菲律宾——强大的糖业资产阶级在政治中发挥重要作用，因此其利益受到贸易壁垒和补贴的保护。
sentences.explanation: 两处短横线夹出地区范围的补充说明。主干用and连接played...与their interests were protected...；their指糖业资产阶级，consequently明确表现书评所概括的因果关系。not just...but...too扩大适用地区，并不意味着世界所有地区都完全一样。

sentences.text: In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse.
sentences.translation: 在争夺行业控制权的斗争中，最终遭遇更不利处境的，必然是那些贫穷国家。
sentences.explanation: In the battle...交代竞争情境；it was...which...是强调结构，突出承受不利结果的poor countries。came off worse描述结果，inevitably带有书评作者强烈的判断色彩，精读时应将这种概括与中性的统计描述区分。

cases.title: The World of Sugar｜工业化、消费与作者立场

paragraphs.label: 原文第6段
paragraphs.text: But sugar production was never just a matter of agriculture. It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam. Further processes involved boiling (from the 19th century, this often involved vacuum systems) and the separation of sugar from other materials in a process known as refinement. From very early on, sugar production was an energy-intensive industrial process, mostly taking place in the countryside and in refineries in centres of consumption, both small and large. The growth of the industry entailed a very rapid diffusion of ideas and techniques from one country to another. Cuba, for example, developed an extraordinarily dense system of railways to transport workers and cane, as well as steam-powered sugar factories. Particular varieties of cane sugar and beet sugar spread very rapidly across the world, in accordance with local needs and demands.

paragraphs.label: 原文第7段
paragraphs.text: Where once only tiny quantities of sugar could be produced, now new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical. Over the same time, there has been a massive increase in consumption. Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy. But as the consumption of sugar has increased, so has the harm it does, whether to people's teeth or weight. In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about. The sugar industry has a history of attacking its critics and, when it comes to obesity, of trying to blame fats, and lack of exercise and self-control. And the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening. High-fructose corn syrup made from maize using an enzymatic process invented in Japan in the 1960s has a similar number of calories to table sugar but is far cheaper to produce. It is now widely consumed, having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods, and is regarded as a leading cause of obesity.

paragraphs.label: 原文第8段
paragraphs.text: This is a wonderfully rich book, a model of global history, the history of production and the history of capitalism. Bosma avoids outbursts of emotion, celebratory or critical, even if they might have made his analysis of the multiple tragedies involving sugar all the more powerful. He shows that we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness. Yet many of the poorest people in the world still depend on it to make a living.

questions.prompt: In the final paragraph, what does the reviewer suggest is the overall message of Bosma's book?
questions.evidence: we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness
questions.explanation: 前文解释危害，末段强调可不依赖糖与替代来源，A概括全书结论。末句贫困者生计不等于作者主张继续扩大糖业。
options: A Sugar is a harmful and unnecessary product.
B Economic pressure is needed to control sugar production.
C Conditions for workers in sugar production should be improved.
D Intensive marketing of sugar has had disastrous consequences.

questions.prompt: Sugar has now become available in large quantities due to a range of agricultural developments.
questions.evidence: new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical
questions.explanation: new techniques等列举支持农业变化让糖大量普及；ubiquitous为无处不在。

questions.prompt: Advertisers initially marketed sugar as a luxury product.
questions.evidence: Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy.
questions.explanation: 过去被视为奢侈品，不等于广告商当时把它作为奢侈品营销；全文无该营销主体与初始策略信息。

questions.prompt: The invention of high-fructose corn syrup was a positive development.
questions.evidence: the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening
questions.explanation: 作者用worrying并关联肥胖，明确与positive相反；便宜只是事实，不代表作者支持。

questions.prompt: High-fructose corn syrup is an ingredient in many processed foods.
questions.evidence: having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods
questions.explanation: adopted in the making对应is an ingredient；many对应a large number。

structure: 书评从糖的种植转向提炼、能源和技术传播，再追踪大规模生产如何与消费增长及健康争议相连。结尾保留一个现实张力：人们可以减少对糖的依赖，但许多贫困生产者仍依靠糖业谋生。
原文第6段：糖不仅是农作物，还需要提取蔗糖、煮制和精炼，这些环节很早就依赖机械与能源。生产既在乡村进行，也在消费中心的精炼厂进行。行业扩张还推动技术、品种和运输设施跨国传播，古巴的密集铁路与蒸汽糖厂是例子。作者借此打破农业与工业截然分开的想象，同时强调不同地方会按照自身需要采用技术。
原文第7段：新的技术、品种、肥料和灌溉使糖从少量奢侈品变成普遍消费品，也被宣传为能量来源。书评随后转向消费增加带来的牙齿和体重问题，以及糖业阻挠减糖、转移责任的争议。末尾介绍高果糖玉米糖浆：热量与食糖相近，生产成本却低得多，因此被广泛用于饮料和加工食品；作者也转述了其与肥胖有关的评价。这是书评中的论述，不能把所有体重问题归于单一成分，也不能把文中now和recent past当成今日实时信息。
原文第8段：结尾高度评价全书的全球史、生产史和资本主义史视角，同时指出Bosma克制了赞颂或批判的情绪表达。作者认为更强烈的情绪可能增强悲剧分析的冲击力，这是一种书评判断。最后的Yet重新引入生产者：即使消费者有其他甜味来源，许多穷人仍靠糖业生活，因此减少消费与保障生计需要一起被看见。

phrases.meaning: 一种耗能密集的工业过程
phrases.explanation: energy-intensive说明单位活动需要较多能源，industrial process指多环节加工；不能仅因原料来自农田就忽略加工环节。

phrases.phrase: in accordance with local needs and demands
phrases.explanation: in accordance with表示与某种要求一致；这里说明技术和品种的传播并非各地完全相同。
increase in后接发生增长的指标；massive是强程度词，实际写作中应与有依据的规模判断相配。

phrases.meaning: 一种有价值的能量来源
phrases.explanation: 在本文中位于was promoted as之后，属于曾经的宣传定位，不等同于作者无条件推荐增加糖摄入。

phrases.phrase: depend on it to make a living
phrases.explanation: depend on说明经济依赖，to make a living解释依赖的目的；it指糖及糖业相关生产。

sentences.text: It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam.
sentences.translation: 糖的生产还包括在收获地点附近从糖料作物中提取蔗糖，这个过程需要由人力、畜力、风力或蒸汽驱动的机械。
sentences.explanation: It指糖的生产。extraction of sucrose from the sugar plant是一个完整名词结构，中间插入close to the place of harvest补充地点；a process是对提取活动的同位说明。which修饰process，powered by...是过去分词短语修饰machinery，列出动力来源而非四个必须依次经过的阶段。

sentences.text: In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about.
sentences.translation: 面对糖业对降低消费努力的严重阻挠，一些国家不得不对糖征税，以促成消费的减少。
sentences.explanation: In the face of引出阻力背景；from the sugar industry说明阻挠来自谁，to attempts...说明受到阻挠的是哪类尝试。主干是some countries have been forced to tax sugar。that回指reduce consumption，in order to表达政策目的，不能单凭这个目的就判断政策效果已经实现。appalling保留了书评的批评态度。

cases.title: Do animals dream?｜跨物种睡眠研究

paragraphs.label: 原文第1段
paragraphs.text: Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

paragraphs.label: 原文第2段
paragraphs.text: There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

paragraphs.label: 原文第3段
paragraphs.text: But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

paragraphs.label: 原文第4段
paragraphs.text: That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

questions.prompt: Research into sleep and dreaming — 1 __________: similar brain patterns were observed when active and sleeping; indicative of dreaming
questions.evidence: the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep
questions.explanation: 表格此行要求动物类别；清醒走迷宫与REM睡眠对比的是rats。

questions.prompt: Pigeons: when sleeping, pigeons displayed activity in parts of the brain that deal with 2 __________ input; may have been dreaming of flying
questions.evidence: brain regions involved in processing visual information
questions.explanation: input对应information；空前deal with与processing相对应，所需形容词为visual。

questions.prompt: Whales and dolphins: still have 3 __________ their brain awake when they sleep
questions.evidence: only half of it, keeping the rest awake
questions.explanation: 只关闭一半，所以另一半保持清醒。句子逻辑转换但数值不变。

questions.prompt: Whales and dolphins: don't experience REM sleep, as this could affect their sensitivity to 4 __________
questions.evidence: during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature
questions.explanation: 原因落在末句；temperature而不是前文machinery或lives。

questions.prompt: Whales and dolphins: their dreams are probably not very 5 __________
questions.evidence: non-REM dreams, which are less vivid
questions.explanation: less vivid改写为not very vivid；保持形容词词性。

structure: 作者从人类的两种睡眠状态出发，逐步追问其他动物是否也做梦。脑活动记录提供了跨物种比较的线索，但动物无法直接报告梦境，所以观察到的睡眠特征与对主观体验的推测始终需要区分。
原文第1段：电极研究表明，人的睡眠在快速眼动与非快速眼动状态之间交替。快速眼动时眼球活动、肌肉可能轻微抽动，但大部分肌肉受到抑制；非快速眼动时身体几乎不动。多数梦境，尤其生动的梦，与快速眼动睡眠相连。本段提供后文比较动物的基础，但most没有把全部梦境都限定在一种状态。
原文第2段：研究者比较老鼠清醒走迷宫时和快速眼动睡眠中的脑活动，发现两者相似，因此推测老鼠可能在梦中重现走迷宫的经历。这里先有脑活动模式的观察，再有对梦内容的解释；开头some evidence和may保留了动物内在体验无法直接验证的限制。
原文第3段：研究非哺乳动物更困难，因为脑结构不同，睡眠中的脑活动也更难记录。鸽子的记录显示两类睡眠状态，并且快速眼动时视觉信息处理区域较活跃，特别涉及飞行等身体活动的影像。作者因此提出可能与相应梦境有关，但suggests、may和possibly层层保留推测，不能直接写成研究人员看到了鸽子的梦。
原文第4段：That said转向适用范围：梦和快速眼动不太可能遍布所有动物。海绵没有大脑；鲸与海豚只让半侧大脑进入睡眠，文中说它们没有快速眼动睡眠迹象，进而推测可能只有较不生动的非快速眼动梦。末句以It's thought提出一种温度脆弱性的解释，属于学术推测，不是确定且唯一的原因。

phrases.explanation: alternate表示两种状态轮流变化，throughout覆盖整个夜间；不意味着只切换一次。
vivid描述体验或画面鲜明，不等于这些梦更真实地反映外部世界。
指获取神经活动数据，不能等同于直接读取一段完整主观体验。
inner lives涉及感受、记忆等内在体验；文中是人类对鲸与海豚的通常认识，而非本文逐一证实的内容。

phrases.phrase: more vulnerable to extremes of temperature
phrases.meaning: 更容易受到极端温度影响
phrases.explanation: vulnerable to后接潜在威胁；more比较的是不同睡眠状态中的脆弱程度。

sentences.text: Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.
sentences.translation: 有趣的是，快速眼动睡眠期间，与处理视觉信息有关的脑区活动较强，尤其涉及飞行等身体活动的影像；这提示，鸽子当时可能梦到的正是这些内容。
sentences.explanation: involved in...是过去分词短语修饰brain regions；related to...修饰images；such as flying给出身体活动的例子。which承接前面整个观察，this指相关视觉和身体活动内容。suggests、may possibly都说明从脑活动到梦内容是推断，what...是表语从句，表示鸽子梦到的内容。

sentences.text: These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake.
sentences.translation: 这类动物包括鲸和海豚，它们睡觉时并不会让整个大脑都停止清醒活动，而是只让其中一半进入睡眠，让剩下的一半保持清醒。
sentences.explanation: These指上文具有特殊睡眠模式的动物。which引导补充说明鲸和海豚的从句；not...but...纠正范围，从整个大脑缩小到半个。it指brain，the rest指另一半；keeping...说明与此同时保持的状态。shut down在这里是通俗叙述，不能机械理解为生理活动完全归零。

cases.title: Do animals dream?｜章鱼行为与研究边界

paragraphs.label: 原文第5段
paragraphs.text: Nevertheless, in many cases REM sleep does seem to have benefits. Growing evidence from birds and mammals suggests that REM sleep and dreaming are important for forming memories and learning. It is believed that when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage. As soon as animals evolved moderately complex lifestyles, they would have needed to dream in order to manage these lifestyles.

paragraphs.label: 原文第6段
paragraphs.text: However, we still don't understand how this outward behaviour relates to internal experience. It seems impossible to know what it is like to be a rat or a pigeon, let alone imagine their dreamscapes. We are quick to interpret the twitching limbs and quiet barks of sleeping dogs, but the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits that comes along with that.

paragraphs.label: 原文第7段
paragraphs.text: Another non-human dreamer offers insight here. In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room. At one point, in the middle of the night, Heidi seemed to dream: her limbs and head moved, and her skin rapidly changed colour, as though she was pursuing a crab.

paragraphs.label: 原文第8段
paragraphs.text: Similarly, a report recently emerged of a sleeping octopus apparently having a nightmare. Costello, as the octopus was called, thrashed around, extended his mantle as if trying to make himself look bigger, and squirted ink as though he were being attacked by a predator. The nightmare study is intriguing, says Scheel, but is only based on one animal. He argues that as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed to show that the octopuses are replaying sequences of activities from their waking lives in dreams.

paragraphs.label: 原文第9段
paragraphs.text: The trouble is that we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams. That goes for other humans' dreams too. But we can try to imagine what these dreamscapes are like by meeting animals on their own terms. For example, vision is the dominant sense for many humans, and so our dreams are heavily visual too. Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.

paragraphs.label: 原文第10段
paragraphs.text: It is likely that dreaming has served multiple purposes since the first complex animals evolved. And if this is the case, it is possible that better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams.

questions.prompt: Dreaming about past experiences helps us to create lasting memories of them.
questions.evidence: when events are replayed in dreams, this helps to integrate memories into longer-term storage
questions.explanation: replayed events是过去经历，longer-term storage对应lasting memories。

questions.prompt: It is now possible to tell what type of dream a dog is having.
questions.evidence: the truth is that we don't know if there is an internal experience of chasing rabbits
questions.explanation: 行为可以被观察，但不知道狗的内部体验，直接否定“现在可以判断梦类型”。

questions.prompt: David Scheel's documentary was influential on other research into the sleeping patterns of octopuses.
questions.evidence: In 2019, while making a documentary, David Scheel of Alaska Pacific University in the USA housed an octopus named Heidi in a tank in his living room.
questions.explanation: 只说明拍摄纪录片时的观察；后续另一报告不等于受其影响，全文没有研究之间的影响关系。

questions.prompt: While it was asleep, the octopus called Costello reacted as if it was hunting.
questions.evidence: as though he were being attacked by a predator
questions.explanation: Costello表现为被捕食者攻击，题干hunting把角色反转；前一只Heidi才像追逐螃蟹。

questions.prompt: Scheel believes more research into octopuses' dreams should be carried out.
questions.evidence: as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed
questions.explanation: 需要脑成像来核验行为解释，说明更多研究仍有必要。

questions.prompt: We may soon be able to share the dreams of other human beings.
questions.evidence: we will never be able to experience any animal's dreams. That goes for other humans' dreams too.
questions.explanation: never与soon be able相反，后句明确将结论扩展到其他人类。

questions.prompt: Hearing may be an important part of the dreams of some animals.
questions.evidence: Dogs primarily navigate the world using smell while spiders rely much more on vibrations.
questions.explanation: 该段举视觉、嗅觉、振动，但没有讨论hearing在梦中的地位；不能自行把振动等同听觉。

questions.prompt: Interest in the reasons why humans dream has increased greatly in recent times.
questions.evidence: better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams
questions.explanation: 全文谈研究前景，没有比较近期与过去关注度，故不存在increased greatly的依据。

cases.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information? TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。原题Q6–13；NG对照完整原篇后确认，未用裁切缺失信息制造答案。

structure: 文章先提出梦可能帮助记忆与学习，再用章鱼睡眠行为展示观察的吸引力与局限。结尾提醒我们从动物自身的感官世界理解梦，并把跨物种研究作为理解人类梦境的一条可能路径。
原文第5段：鸟类和哺乳动物的证据逐渐支持快速眼动与梦对记忆、学习有重要作用。一种解释认为，梦中重现事件有助于把记忆整合到较长期储存中。关于复杂生活方式促使动物需要梦的说法仍带有推断性；it is believed和would have needed都不是对进化过程的直接录像式描述。
原文第6段：However明确区分外在行为与内在体验：我们容易把睡着的狗抽动和轻吠想象成追逐兔子，但其实不知道它是否真的有这种梦境。人甚至难以知道作为老鼠或鸽子的体验是什么样，更不用说具体的梦世界。这段不是否认动物会做梦，而是限制人类解释行为时可以声称知道多少。
原文第7段：作者引入2019年章鱼Heidi的观察。它睡眠时肢体、头部活动，皮肤迅速变色，看起来像在追螃蟹。seemed和as though表明这是依据行为作出的类比，而不是已确认章鱼确实梦到了某只螃蟹。
原文第8段：另一只章鱼Costello出现剧烈扭动、伸展外套膜和喷墨，看起来像应对捕食者，因此被描述为可能做噩梦。Scheel认为这很有趣，却指出观察只涉及一只动物，还需要脑成像来支持梦中重演清醒活动的解释。本段将令人印象深刻的个例，与形成更稳固认识所需的证据区分。
原文第9段：作者承认，人无法直接进入其他动物甚至其他人的梦，但可以从物种自己的感官特点出发想象其体验。人类多依赖视觉，狗依赖嗅觉，蜘蛛较依赖振动，因此不能把所有动物的梦都想成一段人类式视觉电影。on their own terms要求尊重不同物种的生活方式。
原文第10段：结尾提出，梦自复杂动物演化以来可能承担了多种功能；如果如此，更好地理解这些功能也许能帮助理解人类的梦。likely、if、possible和might层层保留条件，作者以开放的研究方向收尾，而没有给出唯一且最终的梦的用途。

phrases.explanation: 两个动名词并列，说明研究讨论的功能；本段说证据逐渐支持相关作用，并未给出适用于所有物种的统一机制。

phrases.meaning: 把记忆整合进较长期的储存
phrases.explanation: integrate...into...表示并入某个系统或结构，longer-term是相对较长期，并非永不遗忘。
as well as在此补充另一类所需证据，后面提出脑成像；不是说行为观察毫无价值。

phrases.meaning: 从它们自身的条件和生活方式出发
phrases.explanation: their指动物，强调不要只套用人类的感官经验；此处不是交易或谈判中的条款。

phrases.meaning: 帮助解释、增进对……的理解
phrases.explanation: 这是照亮的比喻，常用于研究贡献；比prove更克制，不表示一次研究已经解决全部问题。

sentences.text: He argues that as well as outward behaviour, brain imaging is needed to show that the octopuses are replaying sequences of activities from their waking lives in dreams.
sentences.translation: 他认为，除了外在行为，还需要脑成像来显示章鱼是否在梦中重演清醒生活中的一连串活动。
sentences.explanation: He指Scheel；argues that标明这是他的研究判断。主句内容是brain imaging is needed，as well as...补充已有的行为证据。to show说明成像的目的，后面的that从句是待支持的解释；from their waking lives修饰activities，与in dreams形成清醒经历和梦中重演的关系。原文并不是说成像证据已经取得。

sentences.text: And if this is the case, it is possible that better understanding of these purposes might shed light on the true purpose of our own dreams.
sentences.translation: 如果情况确实如此，那么更好地理解这些功能，或许能帮助我们理解自身梦境的真正用途。
sentences.explanation: this is the case回指上一句梦可能自复杂动物出现以来承担多种功能。it是形式主语，that从句给出真正内容；better understanding是该从句主语，these purposes指梦的多种功能。if、possible、might共同保留条件和不确定性，不能把整句改述为研究已经确定人类做梦的目的。

cases.title: Mapungubwe｜农业、居所与社会等级

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A Mapungubwe, which was one of the first states in southern Africa, was formed by Bantu-speaking peoples who were farmers. The area controlled by the rulers of Mapungubwe had at its heart a large sandstone plateau, which was easily defended due to its inaccessibility. As with other kingdoms in the region of southern Africa, cattle herding and other types of farming brought plenty of food and a surplus that could be traded for needed goods. Archaeology has revealed extensive layers of bones and manure, which indicate that from the 9th century CE there were large cattle herds, the traditional source of political power in southern African communities. The archaeological record for the 10th century shows a marked increase in the number of domesticated cattle in the area as well as cotton cultivation and weaving, as indicated by abundant finds of spindle whorls.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: B The total population of Mapungubwe at its peak in the mid-13th century was around 5,000 people. The chief or king of Mapungubwe was likely the wealthiest individual in the society, and would have owned more cattle and precious materials than anyone else. The king and his advisers dwelt in a stone enclosure composed of stone walls and housing built on the highest level of the community's territory, a natural sandstone hill which is some 30 metres high and 100 metres in length. Occupation on the hill dates from the 11th century and the entire complex was surrounded by a wooden palisade*, as indicated by postholes made in the rock. The rest of the community lived in mud and thatch housing spread out below the hill, although there is one stone structure here. This settlement, known as Babandyanalo, covers around 5 hectares (12.3 acres) and predates the hilltop structures.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: C The kings of Mapungubwe were buried at the top of the hill site in a demarcated area away from the dwellings, while other members of the community were buried at the surrounding valley level. A wooden staircase connected the two levels, the sockets for the steps being clearly visible in the sandstone cliff face. There were some grander residences dotted around the outskirts of Babandyanalo, and these probably belonged to male relatives of the king. There are many other smaller but still impressive sites across the Mapungubwe plateau, which are located anywhere from 15 to 100 kilometres from the major hill site. Containing stone residences and walls, they likely belonged to local chiefs who acted as servants to the king.

questions.prompt: a mention of the location where members of the king's family are thought to have lived
questions.evidence: grander residences dotted around the outskirts of Babandyanalo, and these probably belonged to male relatives of the king
questions.explanation: male relatives对应king’s family；地点是outskirts，不能把国王hilltop宫殿当成亲属居所。

questions.prompt: an estimate of the size to which the Mapungubwe community grew
questions.evidence: The total population of Mapungubwe at its peak in the mid-13th century was around 5,000 people
questions.explanation: size指人口规模，peak与around表示高峰估计值；不是面积5 hectares。

questions.prompt: a mention of agricultural produce being exchanged for other items
questions.evidence: a surplus that could be traded for needed goods
questions.explanation: 农牧业产生剩余→交换所需物品，traded对应exchanged。

cases.instructions: Which paragraph contains the following information? Write A–G. 保留完整原候选字母；本片段为A–C，C跨PDF43–44页连续接回。

structure: 文章借农业遗存、住宅位置与墓地分布重建Mapungubwe的社会结构。食物盈余支持贸易，牛群与权力相关，高低不同的居所和埋葬地点则展示社会等级；部分身份判断来自考古推测，保留likely和probably的限度。
A：Mapungubwe由说班图语、从事农业的人群建立，控制区域以难以接近、易于防守的砂岩高地为中心。畜牧和种植带来食物盈余，可用于交换物资。骨骼、粪便和纺轮等遗存支持关于牛群、棉花种植及织布的认识，牛在当地传统中也与政治权力相连。作者把地理条件、生产能力和国家形成放在同一背景中。
B：13世纪中叶鼎盛时，人口约为5000。国王可能拥有最多的牛和珍贵物品，他与顾问居住在高处石墙围成的建筑群，普通居民住在山下泥土与茅草房中。岩石柱洞提供木栅栏存在的线索。山下Babandyanalo聚落早于山顶建筑，这说明空间上的高低与建筑形成的先后是不同维度，不能把山上自动理解为最早居住区。
C：社会等级也延续到墓地：国王葬在山顶划定区域，其他居民葬在周围谷地，两层由木梯连接。山下外围较大的住宅可能属于男性王族，远处较小但精致的石筑遗址可能属于侍奉国王的地方首领。probably和likely保留了所有者身份的推断性；这些建筑共同提示一个中心与周边相联系的权力网络。

phrases.explanation: due to引出原因，its指砂岩高地；这里困难的交通条件反而带来防御优势。

phrases.phrase: a surplus that could be traded
phrases.explanation: surplus指超过自身即时需要的部分，could表明交换的可能性；不是所有产出都拿去交易。

phrases.phrase: a marked increase in the number of domesticated cattle
phrases.meaning: 家养牛数量的显著增加
phrases.explanation: marked强调变化明显，the number of后接复数名词；本段依据考古记录作出描述，没有给出精确增长百分比。
predate是动词，直接接较晚出现的事物，说明时间先后，而非评价建筑的重要性。
dotted around形容分散布局，outskirts通常指聚落边缘；这里描述较大住宅的空间位置。

sentences.text: The archaeological record for the 10th century shows a marked increase in the number of domesticated cattle in the area as well as cotton cultivation and weaving, as indicated by abundant finds of spindle whorls.
sentences.translation: 10世纪的考古记录显示，当地家养牛的数量明显增加，同时出现棉花种植和织布活动，丰富的纺轮发现提供了相关线索。
sentences.explanation: 主语是The archaeological record，shows后并列牛群增加与棉花种植、织布两类信息。as well as用于增补，末尾as indicated by...说明证据关系；纺轮直接支持的是纺织活动，不应机械理解成纺轮证明了牛群数量。for the 10th century限定记录所属时期。

sentences.text: The king and his advisers dwelt in a stone enclosure composed of stone walls and housing built on the highest level of the community's territory, a natural sandstone hill which is some 30 metres high and 100 metres in length.
sentences.translation: 国王和他的顾问住在由石墙与房屋组成的围区里，建筑位于聚落领地的最高处，也就是一座大约高30米、长100米的天然砂岩山丘上。
sentences.explanation: 主干是The king and his advisers dwelt in a stone enclosure。composed of...与built on...逐层补充围区的构成和位置；a natural sandstone hill对最高处作同位说明。which修饰hill，some在数字前表示约数而非一些山丘。

cases.title: Mapungubwe｜贸易、器物与衰落

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: D The Mapungubwe plateau has a very high number of carnivore animal remains and ivory splinters, suggesting that the skins of these large animals and ivory elephant tusks were accumulated, probably for trade with coastal areas reached by the Limpopo River. The presence of glass beads, almost certainly from India, indicate there was trade of some sort with other states on the coast who, in turn, traded with merchants travelling from India by sea. Mapungubwe also benefitted from locally-sourced copper and the gold trade as it passed from the kingdom of Great Zimbabwe (12-15th century), situated to the north of Mapungubwe, to the coastal city of Kosala. It is likely that trade links led to a strengthening of political authority in order to control and even monopolise these lucrative interregional connections.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: E Archaeological discoveries reveal that pottery was produced on a scale large enough to suggest the presence of professional potters, and is another indicator of the prosperity of Mapungubwe society. Archaeological finds include spherical vessels with short necks, beakers, and bowls, many of which have decorative stamps. There are also ceramic discs, and whistles. In addition, cattle, sheep, and goat figurines, and small figures of highly stylised humans with elongated bodies and short limbs have been found. The figures may have been used in ceremonies as offerings to ancestors, but their precise function is not known. Other discoveries include small jewellery items made from locally sourced copper.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: F Beautifully decorated artefacts made of gold have also been found at Mapungubwe. A type of decoration, found nowhere else except Great Zimbabwe, involved the crafting of gold into small rectangular sheets and carving geometrical patterns into it. These sheets were then used to cover wooden objects (which have not survived) using small tacks, also made of gold. One such object that has been discovered may have been a sceptre, while additional evidence of local gold-working is a rhinoceros figurine made from small hammered sheets, and thousands of small gold beads. These objects were all found at the royal burial site and date to c. 1150. They are the first known indicators that gold had an intrinsic value of its own (as opposed to that of a currency) in southern Africa.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: G The kingdom of Mapungubwe was already in decline by the late 13th century, probably because overpopulation placed too much stress on local resources, a situation that may have been brought to a crisis point by a series of droughts. Trade routes may also have shifted northwards. Certainly, the areas that now prospered were to the north, such as Great Zimbabwe.

cases.title: Artificial Intelligence｜公众想象与解决一切的误区

paragraphs.label: 原文第1段
paragraphs.text: In many countries in the West, hysteria about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere. There seems to be no shortage of sensationalist news about how AI could cure diseases, accelerate human innovation and improve human creativity. Just looking at the media headlines, you might think that we are already living in a future where AI has infiltrated every aspect of society.

paragraphs.label: 原文第2段
paragraphs.text: While it is undeniable that AI has opened up a wealth of promising opportunities, it has also led to the emergence of a mindset that can be best described as 'AI solutionism'. This is the philosophy that, given enough data, machine learning algorithms can solve all of humanity's problems. But, in fact, instead of supporting AI progress, this mindset actually jeopardises the value of machine intelligence by disregarding important AI safety principles and setting unrealistic expectations about what AI can really do for humanity.

paragraphs.label: 原文第3段
paragraphs.text: In only a few years, AI solutionism has made its way from the technology evangelists' mouths in Silicon Valley in California to the minds of government officials and policymakers around the world. The pendulum has swung from the dystopian notion that AI will destroy humanity to the utopian belief that our algorithmic saviour is here.

cases.title: Artificial Intelligence｜公共部门实施条件

paragraphs.label: 原文第4段
paragraphs.text: We are now seeing governments pledge support to national AI initiatives and compete in a technological race to dominate the burgeoning machine-learning sector. While many politicians proclaim the transformative effects of the coming 'AI revolution', they fail to realise the complexity around deploying advanced machine learning systems in the real world.

paragraphs.label: 原文第5段
paragraphs.text: One of the most promising varieties of AI technologies are neural networks. This form of machine learning is loosely modelled on the neuronal structure of the human brain, but on a much smaller scale. But what many politicians do not understand is that simply adding a neural network to a problem will not automatically mean that you'll find a solution. Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.

paragraphs.label: 原文第6段
paragraphs.text: AI systems need a lot of data to function, but the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning. Most of the data remains stored in offline archives. The few digitised sources of data that exist tend to be buried in bureaucracy. More often than not, data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed. Above all, the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.

cases.title: Artificial Intelligence｜部署边界、医疗与司法案例

paragraphs.label: 原文第7段
paragraphs.text: For these reasons, the sensationalism over AI has attracted many critics. Stuart Russell, a professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, has long advocated a more sensible and realistic approach that focuses on simple everyday applications of AI instead of the hypothetical takeover by super-intelligent robots. Similarly, Rodney Brooks, professor of robotics at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, writes that 'almost all innovations in robotics and AI take far, far, longer to be really widely deployed than people in the field and outside the field imagine'.

paragraphs.label: 原文第8段
paragraphs.text: One of the many difficulties in deploying machine learning systems is that AI is extremely susceptible to adversarial attacks. This means that a malicious AI can target another AI to make it behave in a certain way, such as forcing it to make wrong predictions. Many researchers have warned against the rolling out of AI without appropriate security standards and defence mechanisms. Still, AI security remains an often overlooked topic when machine learning systems are installed.

paragraphs.label: 原文第9段
paragraphs.text: If we are to reap the benefits and minimise the potential harms of AI, we must start thinking about how machine learning can be meaningfully applied to specific areas of government, business and society. This means we need to have a discussion about AI ethics and the distrust that many people have towards machine learning.

paragraphs.label: 原文第10段
paragraphs.text: Most importantly, we need to be aware of the limitations of AI and where people still need to take the lead. Instead of painting an unrealistic picture of the power of AI, it is important to take a step back and separate the actual technological capabilities of AI from fantasy.

paragraphs.label: 原文第11段
paragraphs.text: The medical profession has also recognised the drawbacks to AI. The IBM Watson for Oncology programme was a piece of AI that was meant to help doctors treat cancer. Even though it was developed to deliver the best recommendations, human experts found it hard to trust the machine. As a result, the AI programme was abandoned in most hospitals where it was trialled.

paragraphs.label: 原文第12段
paragraphs.text: Similar difficulties arose in the legal domain when algorithms were used in courts in the US to sentence criminals. An algorithm calculated risk assessment scores and advised judges on the sentencing. The system was found to amplify structural racial discrimination and was later abandoned.

paragraphs.label: 原文第13段
paragraphs.text: There are some crucial lessons here for everyone aiming to boost investments in national AI programmes. These examples demonstrate that there is no AI solution for everything. Using AI simply for the sake of AI may not always be productive or useful, and not every issue is best addressed by applying machine intelligence to it. All solutions come with a cost and not everything that can be automated should be.

questions.prompt: Stuart Russell's proposals regarding the use of AI are impractical.

structure: 后半篇从专家对宣传的批评转向安全、伦理与实际用途，再用医疗和司法例子说明部署限制，最后提出有选择地使用AI。作者要求把收益、潜在伤害和人的职责一并考虑，并未主张一律停止技术应用。具体项目经历均按本文叙述理解，不作为当前项目状态的独立核验。

cases.title: Miles Davis：独特音色、双重教育与音乐遗产

source.title: British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19
source.originalUnit: British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19

cases.instructions: Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings. Write the correct Roman numeral, i–ix. 本组保留原题号；同一标题不可重复使用。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: At the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Having graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: In the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

structure: 这三段沿着音色形成、学习经历和录音创作展开，解释戴维斯的独特风格怎样产生，以及一部当时反响冷淡的作品如何在后来获得历史地位。个人风格、不同学习环境与作品接受史是相互关联的三条线。
A：A段从十三岁获得小号写起。父亲资助的课程塑造了他的标志性音色：当时许多演奏者偏爱颤音，他的老师却训练他保持悠长、平直的音。后来的自述表明，这种音色成为他认同自身演奏的基础。原文描述老师敲打指关节的做法，是人物经历，不是认可这种教学方式。
B：B段把音乐教育分为学校课堂和俱乐部两种环境。戴维斯不满学校偏重欧洲古典曲目、忽视爵士，因而退学；但他后来仍肯定学校对小号技巧和乐理基础的帮助。与新秀和成名乐手同台的经历，则提供了课堂之外的实践。两种学习来源并非互相排斥。
C：C段将前面的个人风格推进到合作录音。他与其他乐器演奏者创造了较轻、克制、编排更正式的声音，与当时流行的急促节拍和强烈音响形成对照。作品当时缺少赞誉，后来却被视为爵士史的重要转折。in hindsight明确区分当时反响与后来的评价。

cases.title: Miles Davis：困境、跨界与创造力

source.title: British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19
source.originalUnit: British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19

cases.instructions: Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings. Write the correct Roman numeral, i–ix. 本组保留原题号；同一标题不可重复使用。

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Though Davis’ trumpet playing may have sounded effortless and breezy, this ease rarely carried over into the rest of his life. The early 1950s, in particular, were a time of great personal turmoil. After returning from a stint in Paris, Davis suffered from prolonged depression, which he attributed to the unravelling of a number of relationships, including his romance with a French actress and some musical partnerships that ruptured as a result of creative disputes. Davis was also frustrated by his perception that he had been overlooked by the music critics, who were hailing the success of his collaborators and descendants in the ‘cool’ tradition, such as Gerry Mulligan and Dave Brubeck, but who afforded him little credit for introducing the cool sound in the first place.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: In the latter decades of his career, Davis broke out of exclusive jazz settings and began to diversify his output across a range of musical styles. In the 1960s, he was influenced by early funk performers such as Sly and the Family Stone, which then expanded into the jazz-rock fusion genre – of which he was a frontrunner – in the 1970s. Electronic recording effects and electric instruments were incorporated into his sound. By the 1980s, Davis was pushing the boundaries further, covering pop anthems such as Cyndi Lauper’s Time After Time and Michael Jackson’s Human Nature, dabbling in hip hop, and even appearing in some movies.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Not everyone was supportive of Davis’ change of tune. Compared to the recordings of his early career, universally applauded as linchpins of the jazz oeuvre, trumpeter Wynston Marsalis derided his fusion work as being ‘not true jazz’, and pianist Bill Evans denounced the ‘corrupting influence’ of record companies, noting that rock and pop ‘draw wider audiences’. In the face of this criticism Davis remained defiant, commenting that his earlier recordings were part of a moment in time that he had no ‘feel’ for any more. He firmly believed that remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music. From this perspective, Davis’ continual revamping of genre was not merely a rebellion, but an evolution, a necessary path that allowed him to release his full musical potential.

cases.title: Older workers：薪资条件与两种继续工作的动机

source.title: IELTS.org Academic Reading Sample Tasks 2023 · Older workers · Q1–4
source.originalUnit: IELTS.org Academic Reading Sample Tasks 2023 · Older workers · Q1–4

cases.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in boxes 1–4.

paragraphs.text: The general assumption is that older workers are paid more in spite of, rather than because of, their productivity. That might partly explain why, when employers are under pressure to cut costs, they persuade a 55-year old to take early retirement. Take away seniority-based pay scales, and older workers may become a much more attractive employment proposition. But most employers and many workers are uncomfortable with the idea of reducing someone’s pay in later life – although manual workers on piece-rates often earn less as they get older. So retaining the services of older workers may mean employing them in different ways.

One innovation was devised by IBM Belgium. Faced with the need to cut staff costs, and having decided to concentrate cuts on 55 to 60-year olds, IBM set up a separate company called Skill Team, which re-employed any of the early retired who wanted to go on working up to the age of 60. An employee who joined Skill Team at the age of 55 on a five-year contract would work for 58% of his time, over the full period, for 88% of his last IBM salary. The company offered services to IBM, thus allowing it to retain access to some of the intellectual capital it would otherwise have lost.

The best way to tempt the old to go on working may be to build on such ‘bridge’ jobs: part- time or temporary employment that creates a more gradual transition from full-time work to retirement. Studies have found that, in the United States, nearly half of all men and women who had been in full-time jobs in middle age moved into such ‘bridge’ jobs at the end of their working lives. In general, it is the best-paid and worst-paid who carry on working. There seem to be two very different types of bridge job-holder – those who continue working because they have to and those who continue working because they want to, even though they could afford to retire.

If the job market grows more flexible, the old may find more jobs that suit them. Often, they will be self-employed. Sometimes, they may start their own businesses: a study by David Storey of Warwick University found that in Britain 70% of businesses started by people over 55 survived, compared with an overall national average of only 19%. But whatever pattern of employment they choose, in the coming years the skills of these ‘grey workers’ will have to be increasingly acknowledged and rewarded.

structure: 文章讨论怎样保留年长劳动者的经验。先提出薪资和成本之间的矛盾，再用公司安排说明替代雇用方式，随后解释渐进退休的不同动机，最后展望更灵活的就业形式。文中的研究数字属于材料所述研究，不能外推为当前各国的普遍比例。
1：第1段先报告一种常见假设：年长者收入较高未必由生产率解释。might partly把它限制为雇主推动提前退休的部分可能原因。取消按资历加薪或降低晚年薪酬并非没有阻力，因此段末转向改变雇用方式，而不是简单地要求降薪。

source.title: Cambridge Academic Reading official sample · Dung beetles
source.originalUnit: Cambridge Academic Reading official sample · Dung beetles

cases.instructions: Label the tunnels on the diagram below using words from the box. Write your answers in boxes 6–8. 按原图位置作答，词框完整保留。

paragraphs.text: Introducing dung beetles into a pasture is a simple process: approximately 1,500 beetles are released, a handful at a time, into fresh cow pats in the cow pasture. The beetles immediately disappear beneath the pats digging and tunnelling and, if they successfully adapt to their new environment, soon become a permanent, self-sustaining part of the local ecology. In time they multiply and within three or four years the benefits to the pasture are obvious.

Dung beetles work from the inside of the pat so they are sheltered from predators such as birds and foxes. Most species burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels directly underneath the pats, which are hollowed out from within. Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat. These beetles make sausage-shaped brood chambers along the tunnels. The shallowest tunnels belong to a much smaller Spanish species that buries dung in chambers that hang like fruit from the branches of a pear tree. South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat. Some surface-dwelling beetles, including a South African species, cut perfectly-shaped balls from the pat, which are rolled away and attached to the bases of plants.

For maximum dung burial in spring, summer and autumn, farmers require a variety of species with overlapping periods of activity. In the cooler environments of the state of Victoria, the large French species (2.5 cms long), is matched with smaller (half this size), temperate-climate Spanish species. The former are slow to recover from the winter cold and produce only one or two generations of offspring from late spring until autumn. The latter, which multiply rapidly in early spring, produce two to five generations annually. The South African ball-rolling species, being a sub-tropical beetle, prefers the climate of northern and coastal New South Wales where it commonly works with the South African tunneling species. In warmer climates, many species are active for longer periods of the year.

questions.prompt: 原图标号6所指隧道的种类
questions.evidence: South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat.
questions.explanation: 左侧隧道约20cm，匹配South African；ball roller把球滚离粪堆，不能因同国别选它。

questions.prompt: 原图标号7所指隧道的种类
questions.evidence: Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat.
questions.explanation: 中间最深约30cm，与French对应，sausage-shaped chambers补充形状证据。

questions.prompt: 原图标号8所指隧道的种类
questions.evidence: The shallowest tunnels belong to a much smaller Spanish species
questions.explanation: 右侧最浅且分叉如梨树，matching shallowest；不是用甲虫体长当隧道深度。

structure: 这段材料先写蜣螂如何被引入牧场，再从地下隧道、育幼室和滚粪球的位置解释不同工作方式，最后把物种差异联系到季节配合。理解重点是条件、空间关系和形态之间的联系。
1：第1段说明引入过程及建立种群的条件：把甲虫少量分批放入新鲜牛粪后，它们会向下挖掘；只有成功适应新环境，才会形成能自行维持的本地生态组成。三四年后收益明显是文中描述的时间尺度，不能略去适应条件。
2：第2段从共同的遮蔽位置写到不同物种的挖掘形态：法国种向下挖约30厘米并形成香肠状育幼室；西班牙种较浅，育幼室如树枝上悬挂的果实；南非种既有挖窄隧道的，也有把粪球滚离粪堆并固定在植物基部的。文中的形状比喻帮助理解位置，不表示真的长成果实。
3：第3段说明农民为什么需要活动期重叠的多种甲虫：法国种从冬季恢复较慢，西班牙种早春繁殖较快，二者配合可延长处理粪便的季节覆盖；亚热带的南非滚粪球种适应较暖区域。former和latter分别回指前面的法国种与西班牙种。

phrases.explanation: adapt to后接名词性环境；这里是种群能否建立的条件，而不是释放后必然成功。

phrases.meaning: 一个长期存在、能自行维持的组成部分
phrases.explanation: self-sustaining指能够维持自身延续；不能由此推出对生态的一切影响都无须观察。

phrases.phrase: to a depth of approximately 30 cm
phrases.explanation: to a depth of表示向下到达的深度；approximately保留近似性，文中起算位置是牛粪堆之下。
overlapping表示时间有交集，不表示所有物种全年同时活动。

sentences.text: The beetles immediately disappear beneath the pats digging and tunnelling and, if they successfully adapt to their new environment, soon become a permanent, self-sustaining part of the local ecology.
sentences.translation: 甲虫立即钻到牛粪堆下面挖掘、开辟隧道；如果成功适应新环境，它们很快就会成为当地生态中长期存在、能够自行维持的一部分。
sentences.explanation: digging and tunnelling补充甲虫钻入后进行的动作；if从句限定后面的become。they两次都指引入的甲虫，不能把“立刻钻入”与“长期建立种群”当成同一时间、同一确定程度的结果。

sentences.text: The latter, which multiply rapidly in early spring, produce two to five generations annually.
sentences.translation: 后者，也就是西班牙物种，在早春迅速繁殖，每年产生两至五代后代。
sentences.explanation: The latter回指与法国种并列的西班牙种；which从句补充早春繁殖快的特点。annually修饰一年内产生的代数，不是说每次繁殖都产生两至五代。

cases.title: 产品召回：批次、退款与联系人

source.title: Cambridge General Training Reading official sample · Product return
source.originalUnit: Cambridge General Training Reading official sample · Product return

cases.instructions: Answer the questions below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the text for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 4–8.

paragraphs.text: Fancy Foods wishes to inform the public that pieces of metal have been found in some jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Spicy). The batches of the jars involved have numbers from J6617 to J6624. The batch number is printed on the bottom of each jar.

If you have any jars with these batch numbers, please return them (preferably unopened) to the supermarket where you purchased them. You can also return them to the factory (Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown). Fancy Foods will pay $10 for each jar returned unopened and $5 for each jar already opened.

No payment will be made for empty jars, which do not need to be returned. However, the Retailing Manager will be interested to hear from people who have consumed chicken curry from any of the above batch numbers. In particular, it will be helpful if they can give information about the place of purchase of the product.
Jars of Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Coconut) and Fancy Foods Chicken Curry (Mango) have not been affected and do not need to be returned.

Fancy Foods will pay a reward of $10,000 to $50,000 for information which leads to the conviction of any person found guilty of placing metal pieces in its products. If you have such information, please contact the Customer Relations Manager, Fancy Foods Retailers, Blacktown.

questions.prompt: What has been found in some Fancy Foods products?
questions.evidence: pieces of metal have been found in some jars
questions.explanation: 问发现的异物，不问产品名称。三词恰好符合上限。

questions.prompt: Where can you find the batch number on the jars?
questions.evidence: The batch number is printed on the bottom of each jar.
questions.explanation: 是罐底，不是退货地点supermarket。

questions.prompt: How much will you receive for an opened jar of contaminated Chicken Curry?
questions.evidence: $10 for each jar returned unopened and $5 for each jar already opened.
questions.explanation: opened与unopened对应两种金额，empty则不给钱。

questions.prompt: If you have eaten Chicken Curry from a jar with one of the batch numbers listed, whom should you contact?
questions.evidence: the Retailing Manager will be interested to hear from people who have consumed chicken curry
questions.explanation: 吃过产品找Retailing Manager；提供谁投放金属的线索找Customer Relations Manager，勿交换两个身份。

questions.prompt: What is the maximum reward Fancy Foods is offering for information about who contaminated their product?
questions.evidence: a reward of $10,000 to $50,000
questions.explanation: maximum取区间上限，不能取首次看到的10,000。

structure: 这是一份按适用范围、退回处理、特殊情形和线索联络组织的产品召回告示。准确理解对象和条件，比把所有罐装咖喱视为同一种情况更重要。金额、产品名和联络人均属于本材料中的告示，不作为现实召回指引。
1：第1段交代发现问题的产品是Spicy口味的部分罐装咖喱，涉及批号J6617至J6624，批号位于罐底。some与明确批号把范围限定住，不能扩大到该品牌所有产品。
2：第2段说明持有这些批号产品的人可退到购买超市或工厂，preferably unopened表示最好未开封，并非已经开封就不能退。未开封每罐10美元、已开封每罐5美元是两个不同条件。
3：第3段单独处理已经吃完的情况：空罐不退款、也不必退回，但吃过有关批次产品的人仍可向零售经理提供信息，尤其是购买地点。没有退款不等于其反馈没有价值。
4：第4段明确Coconut和Mango两种口味未受影响，无须退回；这与第一段指定Spicy口味共同界定召回边界。
5：第5段转为征集导致涉案人员被定罪的线索，奖金范围与普通退货退款不同。此处联络的是客户关系经理，不能与前面接收已食用产品信息的零售经理混同。

phrases.explanation: 正式告示中礼貌地引出通知内容；wish to并非表示消息还没有发生。
preferably表达优先选择，不是必须满足的绝对条件。
purchase在这里是购买这一行为，place of说明行为发生地点。
lead to后接名词；conviction此处是司法定罪，不是个人的坚定信念。

sentences.text: If you have any jars with these batch numbers, please return them (preferably unopened) to the supermarket where you purchased them.
sentences.translation: 如果你持有任何标有这些批号的罐装产品，请把它们退回购买它们的超市，最好保持未开封状态。
sentences.explanation: If从句限定指令适用的人；these batch numbers回指前段范围。them指相关罐装产品；where引出修饰the supermarket的地点关系。括号中的preferably是偏好条件。

cases.title: Saving the saiga · 生存适应与早期数量变化

paragraphs.label: 原文片段 · 1
paragraphs.text: The saiga, a species of antelope native to Central Asia, once roamed the vast grasslands of this region in enormous herds, many millions strong. Regrettably, such spectacular sights are a thing of the past. Today, the saiga is largely confined to a single country: Kazakhstan. This country is estimated to be home to well over 90% of the global saiga population, with Russia, Mongolia and Uzbekistan accounting for the rest.

paragraphs.label: 原文片段 · 2
paragraphs.text: The saiga is perfectly adapted to the tough conditions of the remote wilderness of the steppes of Central Asia. One such adaptation is its bizarre bulbous nose, which enables the animal to survive the extreme seasonal temperature swings of the region. The swollen nostrils of the nose serve several purposes: they filter out dust and cool the blood during hot, dry summers, and they warm the cold air before it enters the saiga's lungs in winter. Other seasonal adaptations include a heavy winter coat that the saiga sheds when the weather warms up.

paragraphs.label: 原文片段 · 3
paragraphs.text: Despite these superb adaptations to harsh conditions, the saiga has no defence against the threats posed by humans. It was almost driven to extinction by hunters in the 19th century. Legal protection ensured its survival for a while, and numbers steadily recovered throughout most of the 20th century. But the respite was only temporary. In the ten years following the break-up of the former Soviet Union in 1991, over 95% of the global population was lost - one of the fastest examples of species loss ever recorded for a mammal.

paragraphs.label: 原文片段 · 4
paragraphs.text: The dramatic decline during this decade was due to illegal poaching on an industrial scale. Male saiga are a particular target, because their horns are highly prized by traditional medicine practitioners. Poaching reached epidemic levels after misguided conservationists tried to relieve the pressure on threatened African rhinos by actively encouraging the use of saiga horns in traditional medicine as an alternative to those of rhinos. Male saiga were almost wiped out, leading to a population crash from which the species has been struggling to recover ever since.
